heroIntro: Land grabbing targeting absent Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) has historically been an acute menace across Dhaka, Sylhet, Gazipur, Chattogram, and rural districts. Corrupt land cartels, dishonest caretakers, and opportunistic relatives frequently exploit the physical absence of overseas owners by manufacturing forged deeds (ভুয়া দলিল), manipulating manual Khatians, or forcefully erecting unauthorized boundary walls. Fortunately, the enactment of the **Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023 (ভূমি অপরাধ প্রতিরোধ ও প্রতিকার আইন, ২০২৩)** alongside Supreme Court constitutional writ remedies has empowered expatriates with rapid criminal and civil weapons to dislodge grabbers and reclaim ancestral land.

quickAnswer.heading: Immediate Emergency Action Plan for Grabbed Land
points: Gather foundational title proofs: registered original deed, CS/SA/RS/BS Khatians, and e-Mutation records.
Lodge an urgent General Diary (GD) and petition under Section 144 / 145 CrPC before the Executive Magistrate Court to freeze grabbers.
Invoke the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023 for immediate criminal prosecution (penalties up to 7 years imprisonment).
File an urgent civil suit for recovery of possession under Section 8 or Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act 1877.
If police or local administration collude with grabbers, move the High Court Division under Article 102 for a Writ of Mandamus.

sections.h2: The Modus Operandi of Land Grabbers in Bangladesh
sections.content:
Understanding how land syndicates operate is essential for expatriates living abroad. Common fraudulent mechanisms include:

  • Impersonation & Forged Sale Deeds (জাল কবলা দলিল): Hiring an impostor to pose as the overseas landowner before a compromised Sub-Registrar.
  • Fraudulent Record Creation: Fabricating non-existent RS or BS Khatians during survey settlement procedures when the owner was abroad.
  • Caretaker Usurpation: Appointing a local relative, domestic worker, or tenant who later claims adverse possession or creates fake tenant rights.
  • Forceful Encroachment: Erecting tin sheds, brick walls, or signage under political cover overnight.

sections.h2: The Game-Changing Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023
sections.content:
Enacted in September 2023, the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act (Act No. 28 of 2023) drastically shifted legal leverage in favor of genuine titleholders:

Under Sections 4, 5, 6, and 7 of the 2023 Act, creating forged land documents, grabbing land through deception or muscle power, illegal demarcation, or selling land without lawful title are cognizable, non-bailable criminal offenses punishable by up to 7 years rigorous imprisonment and heavy financial fines.

Crucially, Executive Magistrates and Special Courts are empowered to conduct summary proceedings, demolish unauthorized structures, and restore physical possession directly to the lawful owner without waiting a decade for protracted civil litigation.

When grabbers attempt to construct walls or forcefully harvest crops, the first emergency shield is an application before the Executive Magistrate Court (নির্বাহী ম্যাজিস্ট্রেট আদালত) under the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898:

  • Section 144 CrPC: Prohibits grabbers from entering the land or continuing construction to prevent an imminent breach of public peace.
  • Section 145 CrPC: Directs the local Police Station (OC) and Assistant Commissioner (Land) to conduct an on-site inquiry, submit a possession report, and attach the land under police custody pending judicial determination.

sections.h2: Civil Court Remedies: Specific Relief Act 1877 (Section 8 & 9)
sections.content:
To achieve permanent legal recovery through the civil judiciary, two routes exist under the Specific Relief Act, 1877:

  1. Section 9 (Summary Suit for Dispossession): If you or your representative were dispossessed without consent within the last 6 months, you can file a suit under Section 9 solely based on prior possession, without proving underlying title. The court orders prompt restitution.
  2. Section 8 (Suit for Possession Based on Title): If dispossession occurred over 6 months ago, file a comprehensive title suit under Section 8 read with Section 42 for a declaration of ownership and consequential recovery of khas possession (খাস দখল পুনরুদ্ধার) with police assistance.

sections.h2: Challenging Forged Deeds (জাল দলিল বাতিলের মোকদ্দমা)
sections.content:
If grabbers have created a fake registered deed, merely demanding possession is insufficient. You must file a suit under Section 39 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 for the cancellation of the fraudulent instrument.

The Civil Court summons the Volume Book (বালাম বই) from the Sub-Registry Office, orders handwriting/fingerprint forensic verification by CID, and sends a formal decree to the Sub-Registrar to write an official cancellation remark across the register.

sections.h2: Filing a High Court Writ Petition Against Administrative Inaction
sections.content:
Where local police or land administration officials refuse to take action against politically connected grabbers, the constitutional avenue is moving the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh under Article 102 of the Constitution:

  • Seek a Writ of Mandamus directing the District Administration, Superintendent of Police (SP), and AC (Land) to enforce the Land Crime Act 2023.
  • Obtain an immediate judicial status-quo order preventing utility disconnections (electricity/gas) or unauthorized municipal building plan approvals by RAJUK/City Corporation.

Take these proactive protective measures before leaving Bangladesh:

  • Erect strong RCC boundary pillars and a conspicuous metal display board stating: 'This property belongs to [Your Name], Expat in USA/UK. Trespassers will be prosecuted under Land Crime Act 2023.'
  • Never rely solely on verbal caretaker agreements; execute a written registered tenancy lease or caretaker agreement with strict termination clauses.
  • Check the online land.gov.bd portal annually to verify that no fraudulent e-Namjari has been opened behind your back.
  • Pay Land Development Tax annually to generate fresh digital government tax Dakhilas in your name.

faqs.question: Can I recover grabbed land in Bangladesh without appearing in court personally?
faqs.answer: Yes. An expatriate can appoint an Advocate or family member via a Consular Power of Attorney to file criminal complaints under the Land Crime Act 2023 and civil recovery suits in court.

faqs.question: How fast does the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023 take action?
faqs.answer: Executive Magistrates can initiate on-site investigations and issue restraining orders within days of receiving a verified complaint with title documents.

faqs.question: What if the land grabber has already produced a fake Khatian or Porcha?
faqs.answer: You can file an administrative appeal before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) under Section 150 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 to cancel the fraudulent Khatian.

faqs.question: Does paying land tax (Khazna) prove ownership against grabbers?
faqs.answer: Land tax Dakhilas alone do not create title, but they serve as critical corroborative proof of continuous lawful possession and government recognition of your tenancy.

faqs.question: Can the Supreme Court High Court Division order police to recover my land?
faqs.answer: Yes. In writ petitions under Article 102, the High Court frequently issues binding directions to Police Commissioners and District Magistrates to protect expatriate citizens' constitutional property rights.
